topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, the course structure, and the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological basis of cancer as an accumulation of alterations disrupting cellular differentiation and tissue structure, alongside the experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the mechanisms, histological characteristics, and clinical consequences of local invasion, distant metastasis, and the stepwise progression from benign precursors to malignant disease.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature and mechanisms of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the systematic conventions used to name different tumor types and explain the physiological mechanisms through which tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence and multicellularity
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the incidence of various cancers in human populations and across diverse animal taxa as a fundamental vulnerability of multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They review the clinical signs of tumors and evaluate the diagnostic principles, histological findings, and limitations of population screening programmes for various cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It wraps up the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and details regarding upcoming practical sessions.
